learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with fundamental knowledge to perform the necessary calculations for creating simple technical projects of HV and LV electrical installations, while enabling them to continue studying this type of installation in the future through a process of permanent updating.
Understand the constituent parts of substations, transformation centers, electrical installations in buildings, and the essential criteria for their design and calculation.

Raise awareness about the importance of designing electrical installations under safety criteria, highlighting the significance of protections and identifying the most suitable ones for each part of the installation.
Acquire the necessary knowledge to effectively manage electrical installations, contributing to safety and energy optimization.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to high, medium, and low voltage electrical installations
Switching equipment
Protection equipment
Measurement equipment
Control equipment
Protection relays
Types of transformation centers
Parts of a transformation center. Interpretation of the electrical diagram
Equipment and protections in transformation centers. Earthing
Distribution substations: Typology of substations. Busbar systems
Parts of a substation. Interpretation of the electrical diagram
Equipment and protections in substations. Earthing
Protection against overcurrents and overvoltages. Detailed study of short circuit
Protection against electric shock
Protective earthing
Design and calculation of the connection installation
Design and calculation of the interior installation in homes
Electrical installation in the common areas of residential buildings
Electrical installation project in a residential building
Structure of the electrical installation
Particular characteristics affecting the installation. Special premises: public concurrence, with risk of fire or explosion, damp premises
Electrical installation project in industrial or commercial premises

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or cumulative/eliminatory partial exams
Evaluation of practical activities (classroom, laboratory, computer lab, field, visits)
Completion and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects)

assessment_rules: The final grade requires a minimum of 5 points. A minimum of 4 points must be obtained in Activity 1 (theoretical/practical exam) and Activity 3 (project-based learning). If these minimum scores are not reached, the final grade will be the minimum value between the total obtained score and 3.5. Practical activities (Activity 2) and project submission (Activity 3) are non-recoverable in extraordinary calls.
